picks.title: Book Distributor Giant Nippan Sells Books to U.S. AI Developer Anthropic, Japan Book Publishers Association Requests Stoppage
picks.excerpt: A Nippan subsidiary sold Japanese books to Anthropic between Dec 2024 and Dec 2025 without notifying publishers, likely for its book-scanning AI training project; the Japan Book Publishers Association has demanded the sales stop.
picks.rationale: Japan's biggest book distributor quietly sold books to Anthropic for scanning, and the publishers' association formally demanded it stop. This is a new, named supply-chain fight over training data.

picks.title: How much AI is in Spain's bestselling books?
picks.excerpt: EL PAÍS ran 175 popular titles through the Pangram detector: no trace of AI in 2019, but now one in three self-published bestsellers is written mostly with AI, including a top-charting book by politician Alvise Pérez.
picks.rationale: An original data investigation: EL PAÍS ran 175 bestsellers through a detector and found that one in three self-published hits is mostly AI-written. It is hard numbers on how far AI has reached the charts.

picks.title: Publishers urged to join appeal for greater AI transparency
picks.excerpt: More than 150 publishers and organizations back the Frankfurt Appeal from the German Publishers and Booksellers Association, demanding that the EU and Germany require AI developers to disclose the works used to train their models.
picks.rationale: More than 150 publishers have signed the Börsenverein's Frankfurt Appeal for mandatory disclosure of AI training works. It is a concrete industry demand that other publishers can still sign.

picks.title: AI companies' book hunt sparks copyright concerns in Türkiye's publishing industry
picks.excerpt: Turkish publishers warn that AI companies buying and scanning printed books without permission threatens copyright, while some see a potential new licensing revenue stream.
picks.rationale: AI firms' bulk buying and scanning of print books has now reached Türkiye. Turkish publishers are split between treating it as a copyright threat and seeing a possible new licensing income, which shows the training-data hunt spreading to another market.

picks.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Audible-Commissioned Survey Finds Audio Sends Readers Back to Print; Half Would Try AI Narration
picks.excerpt: An Audible-commissioned NielsenIQ survey across 11 markets finds audiobooks pull listeners toward print and e-books, and that about half of listeners would be open to AI-narrated titles.
picks.rationale: A new NielsenIQ survey across 11 markets finds about half of listeners are open to AI narration. It gives data to the AI-audiobook debate where earlier coverage had mostly opinion.

alternates.title: S&S Re-Ups with H.M. Wolfe in Seven-Figure Deal
alternates.excerpt: Simon & Schuster signs a seven-figure romantasy duology deal with H.M. Wolfe, months after The Atlantic cited a Pangram detector reading of 60% AI to claim her hit Daggermouth was AI-assisted.
alternates.rationale: A book-deal story where AI is only background context. The detection theme is already covered by El País.
